title: Johann Friedrich, archbishop of Bremen, to Johan Adler Salvius at Hamburg, Nov-Dec 1631 (Riksarkivet, DECODE R4330-R4331; from catalogue item 207)

steps.what: Fetched the 14 DECODE records of catalogue 207 and their images with the project cookie; found the entry is four unrelated groups. The Bremen 1631 letters (R4330, R4331) are this entry.
Bremen letters transcribed with their interlinear glosses.
Aligned glossed words to numbers: four consecutive numbers per letter.
Unglossed bands fixed from unglossed words (k, z, m, w), then the band order recognised as a six-column alphabet grid read by columns, placing q, x and y.
Every cipher group of both Bremen letters decoded (bremen_decoded.txt).

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 914 tokens, 89 types, de-1640s order 4: reading -2.421 per letter; random keys -6.338 (z 15.2); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -3.647 (mean -3.707, z 28.5); annealer on the real text -3.232. Verdict: pass.

Split from the former catalogue-207 group entry under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): this entry keeps the Bremen band key (R4330-R4331). R4282 is George Lasry's decode4282; R4284, R4306, the Rusdorff letters R4333-R4337 and E 708 (R4338-R4341) are other ciphers, now riksarkivet4284, an R4306 entry (folded on 18 Oct 2026 into George Lasry's contributed sweden4306), rusdorff1628 and oxenstierna1633. Earlier steps on those records moved to their profiles (for R4306, now sweden4306).

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): bremen_transcription.txt (numbers with the glosses of the time) and bremen_decoded.txt (every group deciphered); band key copied from NOTES.md to texts/key.md

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test, 22 Oct 2026): bremen_decoded.txt read through. Every group decodes, but the groups are unsegmented strings with slips inside a '?'-marked clear transcription, and the sentences can be rebuilt only with guesswork from the glosses (48% of sentences clean in docs/_check_reading.py). Both letters relabelled decoded, not read; class read -> not read, method -> not solved, key stays recovered; fraction_read 1.0 -> 0.

Re-reading (REREAD_BRIEF b33): DECODE R4330 and R4331 fetched again with the project cookie; four photographs each, no attachment, transcription, comment or plaintext on the records. One web search for a printed edition: none found.

Clear German re-read line by line on 2x crops of the photographs (many '?' resolved, misreadings such as 'Wir haben nicht' -> 'Wir zweiffeln nicht', 'F.'/'U.' -> the numbers 3. and 11.); glosses re-read (Gr:, Gronsfeldische, Reynacher, Zell, Tillische, dem accord mit begriffen); 23 figure labels corrected on the crops, 8 of them on an ambiguous look-alike digit decided by the gloss (bremen1631_corrections.tsv).

Both letters and the postscript segmented into words, name numbers substituted from the glosses, aligned word by word with the decode (bremen1631_aligned.txt, research/reading_audit/b33_br_build.py: 118 of 132 cipher words exact, 10 clerk's slips read from the gloss, 4 holes, 0 uncarried words), and translated. b17_score de 0.600 plain, 0.843 explicit holes only (before: no reading body, _check_reading 0.477 on the decode). R4330's opening paragraph and one clause stay unbuilt.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.404; polyphony 0.004; 23 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -3.232

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext

Re-reading of 23 Oct 2026: the clear German re-read on the photographs, the figures re-read where the decode slipped, and both letters with the postscript built into sentences and translated (bremen1631_reading.md, bremen1631_en.md).
outcome.fraction_read_source: 23 Oct 2026, re-reading: the one document (R4330 + R4331) reads, so all 955 figures (_check_profile --measure on bremen_transcription.txt, GLOSS lines removed) are in text that reads; inside it 4 of 132 cipher words and 6 name numbers stay holes (bremen1631_alignment.tsv).
outcome.notes: Both Bremen letters deciphered with the band key rebuilt from the clerk's interlinear glosses (about 80% of groups) and the six-column grid order. Split on 14 Oct 2026 from the catalogue-207 group; the other records are separate entries. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: decoded, not read. 23 Oct 2026, re-reading: built into sentences and translated (b17 0.600 plain, 0.843 explicit holes); read.

texts.label: R4330 (27 Nov 1631) and R4331 (2? Dec 1631)
texts.summary: Two German letters of Johann Friedrich, archbishop of Bremen, to Johan Adler Salvius, Swedish resident at Hamburg, pressing for Swedish succour (foot, dragoons, 'etliche tausend') against Gronsfeld's and Bönninghausen's imperial/League troops in Westphalia; he fears the Lüneburg country will be ravaged and asks that the Stift be included in the accord if the Neuenburg garrison marches out. Both letters are in one file each (R4330 and R4331 image sections).

reading_review.note: Clear German re-read on the DECODE photographs; cipher words decoded with the band key on figures re-read on crops (23 label corrections, bremen1631_corrections.tsv; key unchanged) and aligned word by word (bremen1631_aligned.txt: 132 cipher words, 118 equal to their decode, 10 clerk's slips read from the gloss of the time, 4 holes); name numbers 4, 5, 7, 17, 27, 32, 59, 83 from the glosses. b17 de: 0.600 plain, 0.843 explicit holes only; look-alike letters 8 of ~900 (0.9%). Open: R4330 opening paragraph (one cipher word, a few clear words), codes 18, 19, 31, 82, 86, 42.

prior.where: Interlinear decipherment of about 80% of the Bremen groups, written at the time; DECODE status Partially decrypted
